components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Main call-to-action button. Auth/landing use a sharp 5px radius; elsewhere the base Button component defaults to pill.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #EF8450; color: #FFFFFF; padding: 12px 24px; border: none; border-radius: 5px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; transition: background 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: rgba(239,132,80,0.9); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #FFFFFF, 0 0 0 4px #01B990; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Base text field. Pill radius is baked into the shared component, not a page-level override.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; height: 40px; border-radius: 9999px; border: 1px solid #B7C2C2; background: #FFFFFF; padding: 0 16px; font-size: 14px; color: #2E3E3F; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: #01B990; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(1,185,144,0.3); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #B7C2C2; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Pill-shaped status indicator. Color source currently varies by screen; this shows the canonical positive-state treatment.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; border-radius: 9999px; padding: 2px 10px; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; } .ds-badge-positive { background: rgba(1,185,144,0.15); color: #01843C; }

components.name: Content Card
components.description: The standard white card surface used across ~14 admin/customer files.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #FFFFFF; border: 1px solid #EEF3F2; border-radius: 24px; padding: 24px; box-shadow: 0 6px 22px rgba(16, 57, 59, 0.04); } .ds-card-title { font-size: 16px; font-weight: 700; color: #10393B; margin-bottom: 8px; } .ds-card-body { font-size: 14px; color: #2E3E3F; }

components.name: Identity Card
components.description: Elevated gradient surface used at the top of every Admin/*/Show.vue page.
components.css: .ds-card-elevated { position: relative; min-height: 160px; border: 1px solid #01B990; border-radius: 26px; background: linear-gradient(145deg, #55bd99 0%, #0a8d70 100%); padding: 28px; box-shadow: 0 20px 45px rgba(1, 185, 144, 0.24); color: #FFFFFF; } .ds-card-elevated-title { font-size: 18px; font-weight: 700; }

components.name: Sidebar Nav Item
components.description: Active-state nav item on the dark-teal-gradient sidebar shared by customer and admin shells.
components.css: .ds-sidebar { background: linear-gradient(180deg, #10393B 0%, #0D3133 100%); box-shadow: 0 8px 30px rgba(16, 57, 59, 0.18); padding: 12px; border-radius: 22px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; width: 224px; } .ds-nav-item { display: block; padding: 10px 14px; border-radius: 10px; font-size: 14px; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.7); text-decoration: none; } .ds-nav-item-active { background: #01B990; color: #FFFFFF; font-weight: 600; }

components.name: AppModal (signature)
components.description: The product's distinctive default modal shape: a scalloped notch cut into the top-right corner via a CSS mask, with an overhanging circular close button. Simplified here as a static approximation — the real component drives the notch from a conic-gradient mask.

components.css: .ds-modal-wrap { position: relative; display: inline-block; } .ds-modal { background: #FFFFFF; border: 1px solid #C6C6CD; border-radius: 20px; padding: 24px; width: 420px; filter: drop-shadow(0 10px 30px rgba(0,0,0,0.15)); clip-path: polygon(0 0, calc(100% - 56px) 0, calc(100% - 56px) 56px, 100% 56px, 100% 100%, 0 100%); } .ds-modal-title { font-size: 20px; font-weight: 700; color: #000000; margin-bottom: 12px; } .ds-modal-body { font-size: 14px; color: #2E3E3F; } .ds-modal-close { position: absolute; top: -4px; right: -4px; z-index: 1; width: 44px; height: 44px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #10B981; color: #FFFFFF; border: none; font-size: 20px; box-shadow: 0 4px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.2); cursor: pointer; }

narrative.overview: This document captures LeasyBack's visual system as currently implemented — a factual baseline recorded ahead of a planned redesign, not an aspirational description. A prior design critique and technical audit found this system reads as generic/"AI-generated" in places (excessive pill shapes, decorative gradients, inconsistent surface treatment); this file documents what those findings were measured against, so a future redesign has an accurate anti-reference rather than guessing at the starting point. The product identity is built on three brand colors — dark teal, teal-green, and orange — applied with real consistency across both the B2C customer product and the B2B admin product (confirmed: no divergent palette between the two). Where the system is inconsistent is in structure: radius, shadow, card treatment, and pill usage vary from screen to screen with no single enforced rule, even though the color identity itself holds together.
keyCharacteristics: One consistent three-color brand identity (dark teal / teal-green / orange) shared across every surface, customer and admin alike.
Pill/full-radius shape is systemic, not incidental — baked into the base Input and Badge components themselves.
Auth and landing screens use a sharper 5px control radius that the rest of the product doesn't share.
Two shadow vocabularies coexist: a brand-tinted soft-elevation family (canonical) and plain default-Tailwind-gray shadows left over from unstyled components.
A stock shadcn-derived token layer exists in parallel to the brand tokens and is largely, but not entirely, unused.
Single typeface throughout (Instrument Sans); hierarchy currently comes from ad hoc size/weight combinations rather than a small enforced scale.

rules.name: The Unused Blue Rule
rules.body: --primary/--secondary/--accent/--chart-* still carry their original shadcn-scaffold blue and are not part of the brand, yet still leak through on unstyled components like the default Checkbox. Treat as a known gap, not a second valid accent.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: There is no second typeface anywhere in the product — every weight and size variation comes from Instrument Sans alone.

rules.name: The Ink-Tint Rule
rules.body: A shadow belongs to the system only if its color is derived from --brand-teal (rgba(16, 57, 59, …)) or, for the one green-gradient surface, --brand-green. A plain black/gray shadow on a new component is a missed override, not a style choice.

dos: Do use the three brand tokens (--brand-orange, --brand-green, --brand-teal) via their existing Tailwind utilities rather than hex literals.
Do treat brand-tinted shadows (rgba(16, 57, 59, …)) as the only canonical shadow family.
Do keep the pill shape for inputs and badges — it's load-bearing in the base component kit, not a one-off.
donts: Don't hardcode brand hex values directly in new markup — use the existing brand-token utilities instead.
Don't leave a component on the stock shadcn --primary/--secondary/--accent blue.
Don't mix plain default-Tailwind-gray shadows into the same screen as the brand-tinted shadow family.
Don't treat this file's inventory of current inconsistencies as license to add a third variant of any of them — they are documented as known gaps to resolve, not options to choose from.
